description: I use software, AI, Earth observation, and emerging technologies to turn difficult scientific problems into technology that improves people's lives.
summary: TerraTrend Observatory is a web tool that turns NASA Earth observations into an honest answer to one question: is this place really changing, and is the change significant? A user searches for a place or clicks anywhere on a NASA Blue Marble world map, then picks one of six tracked variables: skin temperature, precipitation, surface albedo, soil moisture, 10 m wind speed and solar irradiance (MERRA-2, CERES and GPM-based products). The app pulls 40 years (1985-2024, 480 months) of live NASA POWER data for that point, removes the seasonal cycle, fits an OLS trend with a 95% confidence band, cross-checks it with the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, and gives a clear verdict with its p-value. A plain-words panel then explains how much it changed per decade, how confident we are, and that a trend is not a cause. It answers what is changing, where, by how much, and whether it is significant, so students, journalists, teachers and local planners can move from anecdotes to evidence.
details:
What it does

TerraTrend Observatory lets anyone choose a place on Earth and a NASA Earth science variable, then answers four questions: what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether the change is statistically significant. You pick a location by searching for a city, feature or coordinates, or by clicking a world map built on NASA Blue Marble imagery. Six variables are tracked, all live NASA POWER data spanning the atmosphere, water and energy: Earth skin temperature, precipitation, surface albedo, soil moisture, 10 m wind speed and solar irradiance.

How it works

  1. The Express server requests 40 years (1985-2024) of monthly point data from the NASA POWER API for the chosen location and variable. Responses are cached for 30 minutes, and recorded live data is served as a labeled offline fallback if NASA is unreachable.
  2. The series is deseasonalized (the average for each calendar month is removed), so the long-term drift is visible instead of summer-versus-winter swings.
  3. We fit an ordinary least-squares trend with a 95% confidence band and p-value, and cross-check it with the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope. When both methods agree, the result is much harder to dismiss.
  4. A verdict badge states whether there is a significant increasing or decreasing trend, with the confidence level and number of observations, and the chart shows the anomalies with the trend line.
  5. A plain-words panel explains the finding. Example from the live app: Utqiagvik, Alaska skin temperature rose about +0.58 °C per decade from 1985 to 2024 (p < 0.001, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.76), Mann-Kendall agrees (Sen's slope +0.47 °C per decade), and R² = 0.07 shows that year-to-year noise is large even though the trend is real.

Honest limits

Every result shows its source label (for example "NASA POWER Live API (MERRA-2 / CERES / GPM)"). NASA POWER provides gridded reanalysis and satellite-derived estimates for a point, not a ground station reading. Statistical significance shows evidence for a trend under the tests used; it does not prove a cause, and the app says so on screen.

Benefits and impact

Climate discussions often end in anecdotes: one hot year, one dry season. NASA's archives hold decades of observations, but they sit behind scientific APIs that most students, journalists, teachers and local planners never use. TerraTrend puts those observations and real significance testing one click away and explains them in plain words. We built it in Kisumu, Kenya, and want local schools, community groups and county planners to use it to check claims about rainfall, heat and soil moisture against evidence.

Tools and technology

TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, SVG charts, Node.js with Express, the NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS imagery, and Open-Meteo geocoding. The statistics (OLS, Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope, t-tests, confidence bands) are implemented in our own code and covered by a science test suite. Deployed on Render. Source code: https://github.com/Christian3788/Earth-Science-Trend-Observatory

What is creative

Instead of only plotting data, the tool gives a verdict with its uncertainty and explains it in plain language anyone can read. It pairs two independent statistical tests so a finding has to pass both, and it keeps the interface to three steps: pick a place, pick what to track, read the finding.
